claims.text: Rembrandtplein is a major square in central Amsterdam, named after the legendary Dutch painter Rembrandt van Rijn.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Before becoming a square, this very spot was once part of the city's medieval defensive walls and held a gateway into Amsterdam.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: By 1655, farmers were already flocking here to sell their butter, dairy and poultry, and the area became known as the Botermarkt or butter market.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The square was officially renamed Rembrandtplein in 1876 when a statue of the painter by sculptor Louis Royer was moved to its centre.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: That statue of Rembrandt is the oldest surviving public statue in the entire city and has been officially designated a national monument.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today the square remains one of Amsterdam's busiest nightlife districts, packed with cafes, restaurants and terraces.
claims.subject: self
